A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same relative geodesic representation framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial expansion and reorganization in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original geodesic-approximation, autoencoder retrieval and stitching experiments, vision-foundation-model comparisons, and appendix sensitivity studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds multimodal retrieval, additional baseline comparisons, anchor-selection experiments, runtime measurements and Fisher-metric evaluations.

M1.justification: The core straight-line algorithm, Diet objective and decoder architectures remain intact; RelGeo(Pullback) is renamed RelGeo(L2). Appendix A.4.11 additionally instantiates the previously discussed Fisher approach as RelGeo(Fisher), pulling the Fisher–Rao metric back from output probabilities. This is a limited metric variant within the existing framework.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates image-based retrieval and stitching. v2 adds Flickr30k vision–text retrieval using CLIP text encoders paired with different vision encoders (Section 4.2.3 and Appendix A.4.9), extending evaluation to a distinct modality and correspondence task. Earlier datasets remain covered.

E2.justification: Figure 3 and Section 4.1.1 add fitted linear and orthogonal mappings to the autoencoder retrieval comparison, which previously used only the relative-cosine baseline. Existing stitching comparisons and the principal vision comparator set are retained after matching the Pullback/L2 rename.

E3.justification: v2 introduces fixed-text-encoder multimodal comparisons without augmentation, farthest-point and k-means anchor-selection controls, and timed training and representation-generation experiments. Appendix A.3.7 also specifies an ImageNet train/validation/test subdivision of the original validation set, superseding v1's generic split description. This is a reported protocol revision; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses test sensitivity to anchor-selection strategy (Figures 20–21), runtime–accuracy tradeoffs (Appendix A.4.10), and the effects of Fisher–Rao geometry on classification versus retrieval (A.4.11). Earlier analyses of anchor counts, Diet points, discretization steps and augmentation strengths are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: The new checklist explicitly identifies table summaries as means and standard deviations, and A.4.10 explains cross-model uncertainty aggregation for decoder timings. The previously reported five anchor draws, five autoencoder training seeds and three stitching heads remain unchanged; no increase in repeated runs or new significance-testing procedure is established.

E6.justification: Matched aggregate results in Tables 1–2 and the earlier appendix tables are unchanged. v2 adds baseline curves, further pairwise MRR entries, anchor-selection results, timings and Fisher results. New Flickr30k comparisons report RelGeo(Diet) symmetric cosine MRR of 0.08–0.11 versus 0.01–0.03 for Rel(Cosine) in Figure 6. These are additional results, not improvements to the retained experiments.

T1.justification: Proposition 3.1 expands from curve-length invariance to also address manifold-coordinate invariance of length and energy. Appendix A.1 adds proof sections for the proposition and the distance–length–energy bound, which v1 stated without proofs. A.2.1 also makes the Diet generative assumptions more explicit, substantially expanding the formal treatment.

C1.justification: The principal shared-manifold, pullback-representation and efficient-approximation claims remain. The abstract and contribution list now claim validation across modalities, while the introduction drops v1's 'for the first time' novelty assertion concerning meaningful discriminative-model pullback metrics.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.2.2 qualifies the identical-manifold premise through bounded distortion, unrealistic identifiability assumptions, qualitatively different learned solutions and possible unions of manifolds. Added discussions address implementation-dependent runtime and limitations of multimodal augmentation. Conversely, v1's explicit warning about Diet's stronger constant-scaling and spherical assumptions is not retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-code availability statement and repository link, explicitly specifies Adam for foundation-model heads, describes combining and subsampling anchors selected across models, and supplies detailed runtime information. Most architectural specifications, learning rates, batch sizes, training epochs and hardware disclosures were already present in v1.

R1.justification: The new explanations substantially expand positioning around linear and approximate identifiability, citing Roeder, Nielsen and Syrota, and alternative accounts of learned representations through Brown and Pascanu. Nonlinear ICA and multimodal references are also added. Earlier alignment and geometry literature is retained; merged duplicate references are bibliographic cleanup rather than substantive removals.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the metric-choice explanation, moves and expands Diet background into the appendix, and combines the former separate experiment sections under a unified task-oriented structure. The appendix is reorganized into proofs, explanations, implementation details and results, followed by a new checklist. Terminology and citation formatting are also standardized.

P2.justification: v2 adds multimodal, anchor-selection and Fisher displays plus runtime tables, and expands dataset heatmaps from two to five metric rows. Figure 3 gains baseline curves, and energy plots gain clearer labels. Figure 5 replaces its mismatched MRR display with cosine-MRR values already shown in v1's Figure 13; this is a corrected display, not new performance evidence.

improvement.justification: The strongest gains are in validation and transparency: direct-alignment baselines strengthen the retrieval comparison, runtime measurements make efficiency tradeoffs assessable, and Fisher and anchor-selection experiments test consequential design choices. Flickr30k establishes additional applicability, while code-access information aids reproducibility. The new A.1.2 derivation contains length-versus-squared-length errors, and the explicit Diet scaling caveat is lost, but these shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial improvement in empirical support and practical assessability.
